text:
alex: Quick sync on rollout approach for the soft-evict fallback + telemetry gates. Proposal: 3-phase ramp (internal -> alpha tenants -> regional GA) + small A/B on quality signals. Need sign-off on gating metrics and fallback order.

maria: sounds good. can you list exact metrics that will gate traffic increases?

alex: yes. primary gates: p95 latency, p99 latency, 5xx rate, end-to-end token cost per request, and model-quality regression delta (prompt evals). thresholds I propose: p95 < 350ms, p99 < 1.2s, 5xx < 0.5%, cost delta < +15% compared to baseline, quality regression < 1% (measured on canary promptset).

chen: for the quality gate — how are we measuring "regression"? we need the eval harness and a guardrail for hallucination increase.

alex: good call. we'll use the existing eval pipeline (evals-prod) with the canary promptset + hallucination checker (heuristic + small annotator sample). if regression > 1% on top-3 intents or hallucination score worsens by >0.5, trigger rollback.

priya: fallback order suggestion: 1) circuit-break to slowed rate (reduce concurrent tokens), 2) fallback to model-compact (faster, cheaper), 3) region-redirect, 4) full cutover back to stable model. Thoughts?

deniz: agree mostly but reorder: prefer model-compact first (less user-visible latency impact), then reduced concurrency, then region-redirect. region-redirect is disruptive for stateful flows.

alex: ok revise: model-compact -> reduced concurrency/burst limit -> region-redirect -> full cutover. we'll codify as an ordered policy in the rollout config. sample: 

```yaml
rollout_policy:
  gates:
    - p95_latency: 350ms
    - p99_latency: 1.2s
    - error_rate: 0.5%
  fallback_order:
    - model: model-compact-v2
    - throttle: reduce_concurrency_30pct
    - region: fallback-region-eu
    - rollback: stable-model-v1
```

sam: include a temporary header for clients so we can split telemetry by opt-in vs not (X-Redwood-Rollout: canary). makes analysis easier.

maria: A/B details? what fraction for control/variant and evaluation window?

alex: Plan: phase 2 (alpha tenants) will do a 10/90 split (10% users on variant) for 48h with continuous evaluation. Phase 3 (regional GA) will do progressive 25/50/75/100 over days with 24h waits between steps and automatic revert on gate breaches.

deploy-bot: canary-deployment started for rollout-id=rr-soft-evict-2026-03-21 at 1779998905 :rocket:

priya: ops checklist: alerts (p99 latency, error), traces (distributed sampling at 10%), token-cost dashboards, eval-run scheduled hourly, and a customer-ops slack bridge for alpha tenants.

chen: also add a degradation test: simulate 20% slowdowns for 30m in staging and confirm fallback triggers without user-visible errors.

alex: agreed. open items: (1) sign-off on thresholds (maria + deniz), (2) finalize canary promptset (chen), (3) add client header and analytics tag (sam), (4) add staged rollback runbook for customer-facing support (priya). I'll tag owners and schedule a 30-min preflight tomorrow.

maria: sign-off pending small tweak — lower p95 target to 300ms for low-latency tenant segments. otherwise +1.

deniz: +1 on all; will verify region-redirect constraints with network team before GA.

sam: I'll add the header and a lightweight split tag in the routing service. ETA EOD.

chen: will finalize promptset by EOD and add a small human review batch for hallucination checks.

priya: I'll draft the customer-ops bridge template and support runbook.

alex: thanks all. I'll update the rollout config PR and ping for the preflight invite. :thumbsup:
